turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
From the training set, the highest reproducible median efficiencies come from a fairly narrow set of device-physics “sweet spots”:

1. **Mixed FA/MA/Cs Pb(I,Br) absorbers** — better film formation and defect tolerance than Bi/Sb/Sn-only or single-cation wide-gap compositions.  
2. **nip devices with SnO₂-based electron-selective contacts** and high-work-function hole contacts such as **Spiro-MeOTAD/Au** or **Spiro-MeOTAD/MoO₃|Ag**. SnO₂ gives good conduction-band alignment and lower-temperature processing than TiO₂, reducing interfacial recombination.  
3. **pin devices with fullerene/BCP electron-selective layers** and **PTAA-type hole-selective layers**, especially for CsFA/MA mixed-halide absorbers. These stacks suppress contact recombination and have several ~19–20% training analogues.  
4. Deposition methods that promote uniform, pinhole-free films — especially repeated spin-coating — are favored.

Using those patterns, the strongest candidates are:

| Rank | Candidate | Why it is favored |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **c062** | FAMAPbBrI nip on ITO with **SnO₂-np + PCBM-60**, Spiro-MeOTAD, and **MoO₃|Au**. This is very close to the highest-efficiency FAMAPbBrI/SnO₂ training family; PCBM improves electron extraction/passivation, while MoO₃/Au is an excellent selective hole contact. |
| 2 | **c092** | FAMAPbI nip on ITO with **SnO₂-np**, Spiro-MeOTAD, and **MoO₃|Ag**, double spin-coated. Analogous to ~20% FAPbI/FAMAPbI SnO₂-based training devices; MoO₃ protects Ag and improves hole selectivity. |
| 3 | **c093** | CsFAMAPbBrI pin on FTO with **PCBM-60|BCP** and **PTAA/Ag**. This matches the best inverted mixed-cation/halide training recipes, where fullerene/BCP gives electron selectivity and PTAA gives good hole extraction. |
| 4 | **c085** | CsFAMAPbBrI pin on ITO with **C60|BCP**, PTAA-related hole transport, and Cu. Similar to high pin CsFAMAPbBrI devices; C60/BCP provides strong electron selectivity, and PFN-Br can help tune the interfacial dipole/contact barrier. |
| 5 | **c008** | FAMAPbI nip on ITO with **SnO₂-c**, Spiro-MeOTAD, and **Au**, double spin-coated. A clean, robust SnO₂/Spiro/Au recipe closely related to ~19–20% FAMAPbI training devices. |

Final: c062, c092, c093, c085, c008
